name: Greenish Cyan
lede: Greenish Cyan is a vivid, minty blue-green, built from the modifier "greenish" on cyan rather than coined whole.

sections.title: A modifier at full brightness
sections.body:
The 2010 xkcd color survey and a Wikipedia color list both carry this hex, but neither source documents who first paired "greenish" with "cyan" for it [1]. Two very close crowd and web labels, Greenish Turquoise and a web name called Technobotanica, sit within about 2 units of the same swatch, underscoring how crowded this part of the spectrum is with near-identical names [1].

ISCC-NBS 1955 would file the swatch as a brilliant green, nearly 11 units off, and the nearest library neighbor is [[bright-sea-green|Bright Sea Green]] [2]. It reads as a [[turquoise|turquoise]] pushed hard toward green and lifted to full brightness, closer to a highlighter than to the sea [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, holds no painting where this exact green-cyan covers five percent or more of the canvas [3]. Pigments this saturated and this light did not exist before modern synthetic dyes and screens, so the absence is expected rather than surprising [3]. A match would be a computed color comparison, never a pigment identification [3].

questions.q: Why does our archive find no paintings matching Greenish Cyan?
choices: It is more saturated and lighter than old pigments and varnish produce
The archive has no green paintings
The color is only used in textiles
It was banned as a pigment
questions.answer: It is more saturated and lighter than old pigments and varnish produce

questions.q: True or false: Greenish Cyan is the only crowd name for this exact swatch in our data.

openers: Greenish Cyan sits in a part of the spectrum so crowded with near-identical survey names that three different labels land within 2 units of it.
